business_scope.primary_industry_name: Retailing of Smart IoT Devices and Home Automation

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between France and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with respect to Taxes on Income (signed 30 May 1984, amended by Protocol of 26 November 2013)

Convention between France and the United States of America for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with respect to Taxes on Income (signed 31 August 1994, as amended)
Treaty between the French Republic and the Federal Republic of Germany for the Avoidance of Double Taxation with respect to Taxes on Income and Capital (signed 21 July 1959, as amended)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 2016-1691 of 9 December 2016 (Sapin II), codified in Articles L.561-45 to L.561-50 and R.561-50 to R.561-58 of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier); Decree No. 2017-1094 of 29 May 2017; Articles L.223-1 et seq. and R.123-53 et seq. of the French Commercial Code (Code de commerce); Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized or officially certified copy of passport and proof of residential address for each individual shareholder, manager and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority, municipal or civil registry authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority of the country of origin where French recognition is required; otherwise consular legalization by the French Embassy or Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good conduct / criminal record extract for each proposed manager (gérant)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent criminal record authority in the country of origin (for France: Casier judiciaire national or the French probatory court service)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization as applicable, together with a certified French translation by a sworn translator (traducteur assermenté)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of corporate existence / extract of the company register of any foreign corporate shareholder and corporate director or representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company registry of the country of incorporation of the corporate shareholder or director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; certified French translation required for the French filing

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney (procuration) appointing the local French representative or attorney-in-fact for pre-incorporation acts and signature of the draft articles of association
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin of the grantor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; notarized French translation and legalization review by the receiving French counsel

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all proposed managers, shareholders, beneficial owners and commercial partners against PEP lists (French, EU and international), OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list and French national freeze measures maintained by the Direction Générale du Trésor. Screening must be performed before incorporation, re-run on any ownership or management change, and periodically thereafter. Any positive match or unusual/suspicious activity must be reported without delay to Tracfin, the French Financial Intelligence Unit. Source-of-funds documentation is required for capital contributions exceeding statutory thresholds and for any unusual transaction.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises (GUF) at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; name availability verification also available through INPI Data (data.inpi.fr) and Infogreffe (www.infogreffe.fr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All corporate and registration filings must be in the French language. A proposed company name may be composed of Latin-script characters; where the name originates in a non-Latin script or alphabet, a statutory French transliteration must be used for registration, publication and all official documents. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing French company name, registered trademark or protected sign.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: France / République française without competent ministerial or administrative authorization
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is refused, the applicant must first request a written, reasoned decision from the Guichet Unique/INPI registry. Where the refusal is based on identity or similarity with an existing corporate name or trademark, the applicant may file a preliminary administrative appeal (recours gracieux) with the Director General of INPI within one month. If the administrative response is still adverse, a further application may be made to the competent tribunal administratif within two months. Where the dispute is between private parties over prior trademark or company-name rights, the applicant may independently issue a cease-and-desist letter and seek interim relief before the tribunal judiciaire, including alleged unfair competition damages under French commercial law.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is conditionally permissible. A SARL may use commercial domiciliation services provided by an authorized professional business centre (centre d'affaires) under Article L.123-11-1 et seq. of the French Commercial Code. The domiciliation arrangement must include an actual physical French address, mail-reception capacity and professional reception availability. Mere use of a PO box is not sufficient. The domiciliation contract must be filed with the incorporation documents, and in all cases the registered office cannot be limited to a purely virtual or non-existent physical location given the retail smart-IoT business model.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate. For a standard retail/IoT hardware activity with low AML risk, the expected probability of an unannounced physical inspection by the registry, tax authority or social security authorities is approximately 15% during the first 18 months. The risk rises to above 30% where a domiciliation company is used, where there are UBO/PEP red flags, or where customs or product-safety checks are triggered by imported hardware.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate name availability verification and reservation certificate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce / INPI
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff applicable to name reservation requests under the French Commercial Code

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO piercing, KYC and PEP/sanctions screening of all proposed shareholders and managers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External AML compliance counsel / French notary / avocat
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark fixed fee per UBO/manager file

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of SARL articles of association (statuts) and pre-incorporation legal opinion
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark flat fee for drafting and legal review

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille/consular legalization bundle and certified French translation of foreign corporate and personal documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notaires, sworn translators (traducteurs assermentés), apostille authorities and French consulates
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official notarial tariff, translation per-word market tariff, and per-document apostille/legalization fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Blocked share capital deposit attestation issued by French bank (attestation de blocage de fonds)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing bank benchmark fee for capital block attestation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of legal incorporation notice (avis de constitution) in an authorized legal gazette
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutorily regulated tariff based on the number of statutory publication lines

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Filing of the incorporation dossier and RCS registration through the Guichet Unique
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI / Guichet unique / Greffe du tribunal de commerce
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing and registration fees for SARL formation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office domiciliation service for the first year
Preparation and submission of the French beneficial ownership (UBO) register filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External legal counsel / filing through INPI
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark legal fee for UBO declaration preparation and submission

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 (SARL formation, governance and dissolution), with applicable implementing regulations in Book II
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS Registrar) in the territorial jurisdiction of the registered office; inbound via Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises administered by INPI
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts constitutifs of the SARL and Form M0 (déclaration de création d'entreprise)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: A French SARL has no statutory minimum paid-up capital; statutes may fix it freely (e.g. €1,000). Cash contributions must be deposited into a blocked opening escrow account (compte bloqué) at a French bank or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, and released only after RCS registration or on formal refusal. Contributions in services are prohibited; special valuation controls apply to in-kind contributions exceeding €30,000 or representing more than half of share capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The sole founding member of [COMPANY] SARL hereby adopts the following first board resolutions, effective immediately. First, share subscription: the share capital of €1,000 is fully subscribed and paid up in cash, represented by 100 ordinary shares of €10 each, issued to the founding member. Second, registered office: the registered office is fixed at [ADDRESS], France, until lawfully transferred. Third, appointment: [NAME] is appointed Gérant for an indefinite term, with full power to manage, represent and bind the company within the corporate purpose, and to carry out all registration and publication formalities. All resolutions are adopted unanimously by the sole shareholder.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft, sign and notarize the articles of association (Statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding member and, where applicable, a French notary for authentic deeds
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the SARL statutes in French, including legal form, corporate name, registered office address, corporate object, share capital, shareholder rights, management powers and profit distribution. The document must be signed by all partners and, if desired, notarized to facilitate future real estate or in-kind contributions.
required_dossiers: Valid passport or national identity card of each shareholder and the gérant
Proof of residential address under two years
Draft statutes signed by all partners
Lease agreement or domiciliation contract for registered office
Certificate of solvency and source of funds for each cash contribution
Consent of the gérant to serve as manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If irregular, resubmit corrected statutes within 15 days; obtain notarial rectification where formal legal certainty is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit paid-up share capital in a blocked opening account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Banks licensed in France, Banque de France list, or Caisse des Dépôts
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary account in the name of the company-in-formation and transfer the full amount of the subscribed cash capital. Request the bank's certificate of deposit (attestation de dépôt de fonds) and a receipt of blocked funds. The bank holds the funds until the certificate of registration (Kbis) is delivered or a formal refusal has occurred.
required_dossiers: Bank KYC documentation for all shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence, supplement with certified source-of-wealth statements or notarized shareholder certificates within 5 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish statutory incorporation notice in a legal announcements newspaper
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any authorized Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) accredited in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and submit the legal notice containing proposed corporate name, form, share capital, registered office, corporate purpose, duration and RCS city. Publish the notice no more than one week before filing to the Greffe and at least one day before submission.
required_dossiers: Attestation de dépôt de fonds (bank capital certificate)
Power of attorney if filed by a third party
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notice is rejected for missing mandatory references, correct and republish on the same or following working day; delay does not exceed one additional day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit the incorporation file through the Guichet Unique portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises, operator: Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, select the SARL creation flow, upload certified copies of identity and bank certificates, and complete the M0 declaration. Pay the applicable filing taxes and fees electronically. Ensure the legal notice reference (journal, date and issue number) is accurately entered.
required_dossiers: Completed and signed statutes in PDF
Identity documents and declarations of beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The portal issues an automatic query with a 15-day cure period; submitting partners must correct all evidenced fields and re-upload any non-compliant PDFs within the deadline or the application is abandoned.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register with the Clerk of the Commercial Court and Obtain Kbis
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce possessing territorial competence over the subsidiary or branch
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon transmission from the Guichet Unique, the Greffe verifies compliance, reviews commercial capacity, and performs proof of non-condemnation. Once accepted, the company is registered in the RCS and an extract Kbis is issued, effective as of the registration date.
required_dossiers: Copy of transmitted dossier received from Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe raises a material irregularity, lodge an explanatory letter amending the dossier within 15 days; continued refusal may be appealed to the president of the competent commercial court on summary proceedings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration identification, tax and social formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INSEE, Urssaf, Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), Greffe via BODACC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After Kbis issuance, automatically obtain SIREN/SIRET numbers from INSEE, receive VAT identification from DGFiP, and register with Urssaf. Publish the official registration mention in BODACC. Comply with anti-fraud data transmissions and update any opening branch or retail-store declaration with the relevant CFE within one month.
required_dossiers: Bank account details after release of blocked funds
Proof of designated exercice comptable reference date
Store opening declaration for the retail establishment (déclaration préalable d'établissement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If INSEE or DGFiP assign divergent identifiers or fail to create an EORI/VAT file, file an online rectification request with certified copies of the Kbis; the remedy must conclude within 10 working days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing board is applicable for pure retailing of IoT hardware; consumer-market supervision rests with the Direction Départementale de la Protection des Populations (DDPP), and workplace safety with the Direction Régionale de l'Économie, de l'Emploi, du Travail et des Solidarités (DREETS)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No specific operating license is required under French law for retail sale of smart home IoT hardware; the main legal qualification is a simple déclaration préalable d'établissement for the retail premises.

environmental_impact_assessment.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition écologique and the Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) acting under the Code de l'environnement
environmental_impact_assessment.classification_tier: Exempt (Category C equivalent) — retail sales premises are not covered by the operating-facilities nomenclature (rubriques des installations classées) for EIA; however, if in-house warehousing capacity exceeds 6,000 tonnes, a separate registration may be reviewed.
environmental_impact_assessment.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC permitted discharge; retail premises must comply with local municipal wastewater discharge pre-approval for sanitary flows. WEEE/RoHS obligations apply to marketed IoT devices (e-Waste take-back via approved sys-ema; battery labelling per Batteries Regulation; product compliance with REACH and Low-Voltage/EMC/RED 2014/53/EU directives).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For retail premises open to the public (ERP 5th type M), a fire-safety inspection by the Commission de sécurité is required before opening; the business must hold a favorable accessibility conformity certificate and maintain worksite structural load certificates. Employees require a General Occupational Health and Safety (DUERP) risk assessment and a medical fitness declaration for the store manager under French Labour Code.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Generale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), Ministere de l'Economie et des Finances; operational portal: impots.gouv.fr; one-stop company registration portal: formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; e-invoicing portal: Portail Public de Facturation (PPF/FNFE) operated with AIFE/DGFiP; dedicated desks: Service des Impots des Entreprises (SIE) for SMEs and Direction des Grandes Entreprises (DGE) for large taxpayers.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Draft SARL statutes, arrange capital deposit certificate with a French bank, and file through the Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce allocates SIREN (9 digits) and SIRET (14 digits) and issues the Kbis extract. 2) DGFiP receives the declaration of existence from INPI/Guichet Unique and assigns the French VAT intra-Community number (n° de TVA intracommunautaire), format FR + 2-digit key + SIREN, normally within 1-4 weeks. 3) A non-resident gerant/shareholder must appoint a resident fiscal agent for the company's French tax duties (CGI Art. 302 bis AA) and provide notarized certified copies of identity documents plus proof of the registered office (bail de domiciliation or lease). 4) Open a French professional bank account (IBAN), activate the espace professionnel on impots.gouv.fr, enrol for mandatory telepayment (télépaiement) and subscribe to the CA3 VAT filing flow; file the declaration of existence within 15 days of the start of activity per CGI Art. 286.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a commercial SARL is automatically liable to corporate income tax (impôt sur les societes, IS) under CGI Art. 206(1) on worldwide profits; standard IS rate 25% with a reduced 15% rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for small enterprises meeting turnover and profit conditions (CGI Art. 219). Territorial scope is modified by French territoriality: profits attributable to a foreign permanent establishment may be excluded from the French tax base if supported by the relevant treaty and the Art. 209-A mechanism. No pass-through status applies by default; partnership taxation (transparence fiscale) is available only upon statutory election. The VAT small-business franchise is an indirect tax relief only and does not alter the IS classification.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: 1) Election for partnership/income-tax treatment under CGI Art. 239 bis AA (family SARL, SARL de famille) where all shares are held by relatives; election is made jointly by all shareholders and is irrevocable for 5 years. 2) Election under CGI Art. 239 bis AB allowing a small SARL (<=50 employees, annual turnover <=EUR 10 million, professionally managed and capital substantially held by natural persons) to be taxed as a pass-through entity at income tax rates for 5 years. 3) Reverse election under CGI Art. 206(3): a societe de personnes may elect entity-level corporate income tax, irrevocable unless statutory conditions are met. 4) VAT group election (assujetti unique) under CGI Art. 256 C allowing closely linked French group entities to file as a single taxable person. 5) France has no US-style check-the-box; hybrid mismatch consequences are addressed via ATAD I/II provisions including CGI Art. 212 bis, requiring documentation and self-adjustment for deduction/ non-inclusion mismatches and asymmetric branch structures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutee, TVA) governed by CGI Arts. 256-289 C, Directive 2006/112/EC and the 2021 EU E-commerce VAT Package.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a French-established SARL there is no VAT registration threshold: registration is mandatory from the first taxable transaction upon incorporation. The small-business exemption (franchise en base de TVA, CGI Art. 293 B) applies only below annual net turnover of EUR 85,000 for supplies of goods and EUR 37,500 for services (effective 1 January 2025 pursuant to Ordonnance n°2024-1312 implementing Directive 2020/285/EU, indexed annually; previously EUR 91,900 / EUR 47,700). For goods sold remotely to consumers in other EU member states, the EU-wide distance-sales threshold is EUR 10,000 (exclusive of VAT); once exceeded, VAT must be accounted for at the destination member state's rate, typically through the One-Stop-Shop (OSS), which is optional below the threshold. Non-resident sellers without French establishment and non-EU sellers have no exemption and must register from the first euro unless using OSS/IOSS.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France does not apply a Latin-American real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping model; it mandates structured e-invoicing and e-reporting through the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF/FNFE) network. Under the French e-invoicing reform (Ordonnance 2021-1190, Decret n°2022-1299, as amended): from 1 September 2026, large enterprises and ETIs must issue and receive structured B2B e-invoices, with all VAT-registered entities required to receive e-invoices; from 1 September 2027, SMEs/micro-enterprises must issue e-invoices. Invoices must use Factur-X, UBL or CII formats and be exchanged through DGFiP-immatriculated dematerialization platforms (PDPs) or directly via the PPF using REST/JSON APIs; invoice data must be transmitted within one business day of issuance, and e-reporting data (B2C sales and B2B international transactions) is transmitted monthly with payment data reconciled to acquirer records. Retail smart-home IoT sales via Stripe, Shopify Payments and other PSPs will be matched to B2C e-reporting; no government fiscal stamp is affixed, but the integrity chain requires qualified electronic signatures/seals and a 6-year retention period (Code de Commerce Art. L. 123-22).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of physical goods to a destination outside the European Union qualify for 0% TVA under CGI Art. 262-I provided the goods physically leave EU customs territory within 90 days of the supply (CGI Art. 269-3) and the vendor holds the customs export declaration (EX/MRN) together with transport and payment evidence. Intra-Community supplies to VAT-registered EU businesses qualify as exempt under CGI Art. 262-II when the buyer's EU VAT number is obtained, the goods are dispatched to another member state, and the recapitulative statement (DEB/EC Sales List) is filed on time; for EU B2C distance sales, destination taxation through OSS is required above the EUR 10,000 threshold. Supplies of offshore services to non-EU business customers are generally outside the scope of French VAT (CGI Art. 259-0); services physically rendered on IoT hardware located in France at the time of performance (installation, repairs, configuration) remain French-vatable under CGI Art. 259-A(2) unless the service is directly linked to the export of the goods, in which case 0% may be claimed with equivalent documentary substantiation. Unsupported zero-rating carries full liability for 20% French VAT, penalties and interest.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: MRN (Movement Reference Number) and DELTA-X/DX export summary declaration evidencing physical exit from EU territory within the 90-day statutory window (CGI Art. 269-3)

Commercial invoice, packing list, transport contract (CMR/AWB/Bill of Lading), buyer's EU VAT ID for intra-Community supplies, DEB/EC Sales List filing acknowledgment, and proof of exchange repatriation or equivalent banking evidence
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP reconciles export zero-rating claims against customs DELTA-X MRN data, DEB/VIES sales lists, e-reporting files and bank remittance records. A failure to produce customs proof of exit within 90 days, or the absence of inward FX repatriation within the 180-day deadline, triggers recharacterization of the transaction as a French taxable retail or domestic supply, with assessment of 20% TVA plus restitution of any previously credited export VAT. Rectification follows the Art. L. 57 LPF procedure (proposition de rectification with a 30-day response period) within the standard 3-year statute of limitation (Art. L. 169 LPF). Penalties: CGI Art. 1729 imposes a 40% increase for intentional inaccuracy and 80% for abusive manoeuvres or simulated transactions; late-payment interest accrues at 0.20% monthly under CGI Art. 1727; aggravated tax fraud under CGI Art. 1741 carries up to 5 years' imprisonment and a EUR 500,000 fine (up to 7 years/EUR 1,000,000 for aggravated circumstances involving laundering or organized fraud). False customs documentation additionally triggers criminal Customs Code penalties (Art. 414 et seq., up to EUR 450,000 and imprisonment), publication of sanctions, and clawback via the abuse-of-right procedure (Art. L. 64 LPF).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (French Central Bank), acting in coordination with the Direction Générale du Trésor (DG Trésor) of the French Ministry of Economy, Finance, and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty; the regime is codified under the Code Monétaire et Financier (CMF), EU Regulation No 575/2013 (CRR), Directive 2014/65/EU (MiFID II), and Directive (EU) 2015/2366 (PSD2).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France, as a euro-area member, maintains full de jure and de facto convertibility of the euro for current-account transactions (trade, services, income, dividends, interest, royalties) under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and the OECD Codes of Liberalisation. Capital-account operations, including equity injections, shareholder loans, and repatriation of liquidation proceeds, are unrestricted for non-resident investors in a French SARL, subject to the mandatory statistical balance-of-payments reporting to Banque de France for transactions at or above EUR 50,000 per counterparty (direct investment declarations under Article L.151-2 CMF). Profit remittance via dividends is permitted without exchange-control authorisation; the only applicable hurdles are French withholding tax under domestic law (25%) potentially reduced to 15% or 0% under double-tax treaties or the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, and the standard corporate documentation burden (shareholders' meeting minutes, audited accounts, tax clearance). No material convertibility or transfer risk exists: the euro is freely usable, and the SARL may hold multicurrency accounts without restriction. For the target cross-border IoT hardware model, the practical constraint is not legal convertibility but bank-side compliance documentation for large CNY and USD settlements originating from and paid to non-resident counterparties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no mandatory export-proceeds surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio in France. A French resident SARL may freely retain foreign-currency export receipts received from EU and third-country customers on authorised intermediary bank accounts, subject to three cumulative obligations: (i) the underlying receivables must be repatriated to a French or EEA-based banking account within normal commercial terms, with no statutory conversion deadline; (ii) each individual cross-border transaction equal to or exceeding EUR 50,000 must be reported to Banque de France for balance-of-payments statistical purposes via the bank's eco-system or direct DG Trésor filing; and (iii) offshore accumulation of export proceeds is permissible only where there is a bona fide treasury, investment, or settlement rationale, and the funds remain attributable to the SARL in the French tax net. The mandatory conversion ratio is effectively zero percent: the treasury policy may elect to convert USD and CNY export receipts into euro, retain them for future trade disbursements in the invoice currency, or hedge the exposure via permitted forward instruments. For this smart-home IoT retail model, the recommended policy is to convert net euro treasury requirements monthly and hedge the residual USD/CNY exposure.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: High for EEA-licensed electronic-money institutions and PSD2 payment institutions holding a French agrément or a valid EU passport (e.g., Qonto, Shine, Penta, Revolut Business EU, Lydia/SumUp), which may open operational accounts fully remotely and offer multicurrency IBANs, virtual card issuance, and API treasury connectivity. Feasibility rating: Low-to-Medium for offshore non-EEA EMIs (UK FCA-only companies operating post-Brexit, US, Hong Kong, or MENA licences): these cannot provide principal French IBANs and may be treated as unregulated deposit-taking vehicles under French banking monopoly rules, creating legal exposure for the SARL under Article L.511-1 CMF. A compliant structure is a primary operating account at a tier-1 French bank plus an EEA-passported EMI for high-volume Stripe/Shopify settlement sweeps; all balances must remain subject to French accounting and the Banque de France statistical framework. The SARL must also ensure the EMI is in the AMF blacklist-free environment and satisfies the 'Droit au compte' (right to account) fallback mechanism established by Article L.312-1 CMF.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For tier-1 French commercial banks, physical presence of at least one legal representative and the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) is the universal market practice, effectively mandatory under the French AMF/ACPR AML doctrine and Articles L.561-5 et seq. CFM; remote opening is rarely accepted for a non-resident shareholder chain, except at fintech EMIs applying equivalent video-identification procedures compliant with ACPR guidelines. At least one statutory director (gérant) must appear in person at a French branch or be available for an interactive video interview with biometric and identity-document verification where the bank's policy permits remote onboarding. A notarised and apostilled power of attorney may substitute for non-resident co-directors, but the beneficial-owner identification process cannot be delegated: personal documentation, proof of address, source-of-wealth statements, and a short statement of business intent are required. For the target structure, the recommendation is to budget a two-day Paris trip for the gérant and the principal non-resident shareholder to complete biometric KYC, sign the account mandate (pouvoir), and validate the dual-signature scheme.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Failure or inconsistency of the beneficial-owner declaration (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs, RBE) at the French Registry
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified registry extract (extrait RBE) proving timely filing, notarised ownership-chain chart, certified constitutional documents of each non-resident shareholder, passport copies, proof of registered address, and a narrative statement of control for all natural persons holding more than 25% of shares or voting rights.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for the initial capital injection from non-resident shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder bank statements covering the six months preceding the contribution, source-of-wealth statement signed by each UBO, issued capital subscription deed (acte de souscription), bank-to-bank confirmation of the incoming wire, and audited or documented evidence of the shareholder's business liquidity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk or opaque supply-chain structure involving Chinese IoT manufacturers and cross-border ecommerce settlements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed supplier master agreements, customs and import documentation (EORI, import declarations via the French Single Window), Stripe and Shopify settlement reports, warehouse contracts, VAT registration and Intrastat filings, CMR/bill-of-lading records, and a written AML risk self-assessment categorising the activity as standard retail distribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, EU restrictive measures, or dual-use technology screening alerts on trading partners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Screening reports from a reputable compliance engine (World-Check, Dow Jones) showing no match, supplier official business registry extracts, end-user certificates for IoT hardware containing encryption functionality, and a denial-verification letter confirming the absence of EU dual-use export-control flags for the retail product range.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Heavy reliance on digital payment aggregators (Stripe / Shopify Payments) creating perceived reputational and operational risk for the bank
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Platform volume and chargeback history, PCI DSS attestation of compliance, merchant verification records, refund and dispute policy documentation, tax clearance certificate (avis de situation fiscale), and a treasury segregation plan showing daily sweeps from payment aggregator balances into the French operational account.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital injections from non-resident shareholders must be effected through compliant SEPA Credit Transfer (for EUR) or SWIFT MT103 (for non-EUR currencies) into the SARL's designated IBAN at a tier-1 French bank. The remittance information field (Field 70) must openly state the purpose as 'Contribution au capital – SARL [name]' and should be accompanied by a bank-level purpose code aligned with the ECB Balance of Payments framework, typically B320 (direct investment capital contribution) or, for shareholder loans, B321. For direct investment statistics, Banque de France requires the non-resident parent to file a direct investment declaration whenever the capital contribution causes the parent's ownership to reach or exceed 10% of the SARL's share capital (Article L.151-2 CMF); this declaration is statistical and does not constitute exchange-control authorisation. The verification bundle to be retained by the SARL includes: the share subscription deed, the notary or gérant's certificate of paid-in capital, the bank statement showing credit of funds, the SWIFT purpose code confirmation, and a copy of the updated KBis extract. Where the injection includes non-EUR currency, the arrangement should specify the conversion benchmark rate and, to minimise future tax and treasury complexity, effect the conversion at the receiving bank at the ECB daily euro reference rate on the value date.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements to suppliers of smart-home IoT hardware (primarily Chinese manufacturers) require dual-track clearing rails: (i) for shipments below EUR 50,000 or strategic suppliers with open-account terms, the preferred rail is SWIFT MT103 with a compliant 'remittance information' field referencing the invoice number and customs EORI of the SARL, settled in USD or EUR via the French bank's correspondent banking network or via a Chinese renminbi-clearing bank to avoid bilateral clearing constraints; (ii) for high-value or initial trial containers, a commercial documentary Letter of Credit under UCP600 (ICC Uniform Customs and Practice for Documentary Credits) issued by the French bank in favour of the Chinese beneficiary, with Incoterms 2020 rules (FOB or CIF) and customs-aligned invoice values, provides security against shipment risk. The SARL must also use the SEPA instant credit transfer rail for European sub-suppliers and logistics providers. All disbursements require strict dual-signature mandates and a monthly treasury reconciliation against Stripe and Shopify settlement reports. The target clearing currency mix for procurement is approximately 65% EUR, 30% USD, and 5% CNY; hedged as detailed below, with settlement timing aligned to the supplier's 30/60/90-day credit terms.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX Forwards (contrats de change à terme) with a French or EEA-authorised credit institution or AMF-licensed investment firm, hedging EUR/USD and EUR/CNY exposures arising from trade payables and expected export receipts, with tenors of up to 12 months and strict underlying-trade documentation to avoid speculative characterisation under French banking law.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on offshore CNY (CNH) referencing the onshore CNH fix, executed through an international or French AMF-licensed broker, mirroring the hedge of the CNY-denominated procurement cycle where deliverable CNY onshore instruments are not administratively available.

Cross-Currency Swaps (change de devises) matching EUR/USD and EUR/CNY procurement and settlement cycles, including periodic exchange of floating or fixed-rate cashflows, provided the underlying liability is evidenced by supplier invoices and the swap is booked under an ISDA or French master agreement with a licensed financial institution.

Vanilla FX Options (options de change) permitting the purchase of USD or CNY at a hedged strike while retaining the benefit of favourable market movements, executed solely for hedge accounting alignment with the commercial invoice exposure, never for speculative proprietary trading.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval and deposit of annual financial statements (comptes annuels: bilan, compte de résultat, annexes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce (RCS registrar)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' approval must occur within 6 months of fiscal year-end; deposit at the greffe must occur within 1 month of approval (calendar-year SARL: approve by 30 June, deposit by 31 July)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late deposit triggers injunction proceedings and a court-imposed fine up to €2,000; persistent failure may lead to administrative strike-off (radiation) from the RCS and civil liability for the gérant.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale, n°2065 and supporting schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP (administrative tax authority, electronic filing through impots.gouv.fr)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months of fiscal year-end; for 31 December year-end, e-filing deadline is 3 May of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 10% of assessed tax; monthly late-payment interest of 0.2% per month; aggravated fraud cases attract a 40% penalty.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial-ownership confirmation (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Submitted annually together with the deposit of annual financial accounts; any change in beneficial ownership must be declared within 15 days of the underlying transaction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain or declare beneficial owners exposes the SARL and its directors to administrative fines up to €15,000 and possible RCS strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-added tax (VAT) returns and annual reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly or quarterly CA3 return due by the 19th/24th of the following month; simplified-regime annual CA12 return due by the second business day of May
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% plus 0.2% monthly interest; unpaid VAT can lead to enforced recovery and tax-control exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local business contribution (CFE — cotisation foncière des entreprises)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Declaration filed by the second business day in May; principal payment due 15 December of the same year (direct-debit instalment scheme optional)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty of 10%, plus 0.2% per month interest; coercive recovery procedures may be initiated immediately.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit (commissaire aux comptes) is compulsory if the SARL exceeds at least two of three thresholds at the balance-sheet date: total assets over €4,000,000; net turnover over €8,000,000; average workforce over 50 employees. Thresholds must be verified two consecutive financial years. Mandatory also in certain change-of-legal-form cases, for controlling entities, or when ordered by a court.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général — ANC regulations) applying the French Commercial Code; IFRS is permitted only for consolidated financial statements or specific listed groups.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must maintain an up-to-date internal register of beneficial owners. A declaration must be filed with the greffe simultaneously with the annual deposit of financial statements. Every transfer of shares or other event affecting beneficial ownership must be recorded in the UBO register and regregistered at the greffe within 15 days of that event.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Managers (registre des décisions du gérant et des assemblées)
Minute Book (registre des procès-verbaux d'assemblées générales)
Register of Beneficial Owners (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $130-$650 for registered-office or commercial-domiciliation services in France
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $3,200-$16,000 for a certified audit of a small-to-mid-size SARL

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) for fiscal years opened in or after 2022; eligible small companies pay 15% on the first EUR 38,120 of taxable profit.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% small-business rate on the first tranche; research tax credit (CIR) at 30% of qualifying R&D expenditure (capped at EUR 100 million); innovation tax credit (CII) at 20% of eligible innovation expenditure; certain territorial exemptions for foreign permanent establishment profits; tax credits for donations, training and ecological transitions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (annual offset cap of EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of the taxable profit exceeding EUR 1,000,000; a one-year carryback also exists for deficits up to EUR 1,000,000)
